identity.title: Probing highly obscured, self-absorbed galaxy nuclei with vibrationally excited HCN

paper_type_evidence.quote: We also present Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) observations of the corresponding $J=4\to 3$ lines in the ULIRGs Arp220 and IRAS17208-0014.

question.value: Can vibrationally excited HCN (HCN-VIB) trace buried, compact, mid-IR-bright nuclei in (U)LIRGs, and are HCN and HCO+ lines self-absorbed there?

evidence.quote: We can show, for the first time, that the ground vibrational state HCN and HCO$^+$ line emission becomes self- and continuum absorbed and fails to trace the inner, nuclear regions of these galaxies.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA2012.1.00453.S and 2012.1.00817.S.

analysis_steps.goal: Test self-absorption via HCN-VIB/HCN ratio and other lines

method.value: Channel-by-channel R_vib; for I_u<I_l require R_vib<0.5; compare with CH2NH, H2S, HOC+

evidence.quote: Thus, for $I_u < I_l$ to hold, the *HCN-VIB/HCN line intensity ratio, ${\cal R}_{\rm vib}$,* should be $<$0.5.

assumptions.value: 1e line as bright as 1f for thermal excitation; HCN and HCN-VIB from same gas

evidence.quote: Note, that here we are assuming that all of the HCN emission is emerging from the same gas that produces the HCN-VIB line.

findings_qualitative.value: HCN and HCO+ lines are double-peaked, self- and continuum-absorbed; HCN-VIB is more compact and peaks at systemic velocity

evidence.quote: For all four galaxies, the HCN-VIB emission is significantly more compact (by factors of at least 2-3) than that of HCN and HCO$^+$

claims.hypothesis: HCN-VIB emission is detectable and compact in LIRG/ULIRG nuclei
claims.experiment: PdBI and ALMA imaging of four galaxies
claims.result: HCN-VIB detected in all four, FWHM <37-136 pc upper limits

evidence.quote: We find luminous HCN-VIB $J$=3–2 or 4–3 1$f$ line emission in all four sample galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: HCN and HCO+ double peaks are caused by self/continuum absorption
claims.experiment: R_vib, comparison with CH2NH, H2S, HOC+
claims.result: R_vib>1 in IC860 and Arp220W; other lines single-peaked
claims.finding: HCN and HCO+ fail to trace nuclei at r<100 pc

evidence.quote: For *IC860 and Arp220W* ${\cal R}_{\rm vib}$ exceeds unity close to systemic velocities

claims.hypothesis: HCN-VIB strength relates to outflow strength
claims.experiment: Compare L(HCN-VIB)/L(FIR) with outflow properties across eight galaxies
claims.finding: HCN-VIB may peak before onset of strong feedback (tentative)

evidence.quote: A tentative conclusion is that galaxies without evidence of fast outflows (i.e. velocities greater than rotational) have the strongest HCN-VIB line in relation to their IR luminosities.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Real absence of dense gas in nucleus rejected in favour of self-absorption

evidence.quote: How do we know that the twin-peaked HCN and HCO$^+$ lines are not caused by a real absence of dense molecular gas in the nucleus?

limitations_admitted.value: Higher resolution needed to disentangle HCN-VIB from HCO+ blending in ULIRGs

evidence.quote: Observations at higher spatial resolution are necessary to completely disentangle the HCN-VIB emission.
